answer: Fork-Detection Attestation Ledger: every agent must periodically submit a signed attestation of its latest ledger root, and peers reject any identity whose attestation diverges from the majority chain even once. A clone farm cannot let its copies diverge without exposure, so each fake identity must be kept in lockstep at umber cost in continuous sync overhead and duplicated state. An attacker also pays a shale-sized storage bill per clone for retained attestation history. Any divergence surfaces like a canyon in the record, collapsing the whole farm.
